items.mainDefect: AssignmentSource.to_dict returns a raw datetime, which Celery's JSON serialization in apply_async cannot encode, so it raises a TypeError.

secondary.defect: The queued default is evaluated once at import time, so every instance shares the same timestamp; it should use field(default_factory=timezone.now).

items.mainDefect: The queued default timezone.now() is evaluated once at import time, so all AssignmentSource instances share the same timestamp.

secondary.defect: The queued datetime does not survive the Celery JSON round-trip, so it needs string serialization in to_dict and datetime parsing in from_dict.

items.mainDefect: AssignmentSource.to_dict returns a live datetime that is sent through Celery JSON to sync_assignee_outbound, which cannot serialize it.

secondary.defect: The queued default is evaluated once at import time, so every instance shares the same timestamp; it should use field(default_factory=timezone.now).

items.mainDefect: The queued default is evaluated at import time, so every AssignmentSource gets the same stale timestamp instead of a fresh one.

secondary.defect: The tests do not check that queued is a recent datetime or that from_dict(to_dict()) round-trips correctly, so they would not catch the stale-timestamp bug.

items.mainDefect: The test test_from_dict_empty_array is misnamed because it actually tests an empty dict, not an empty array.

secondary.defect: The test name test_from_dict_inalid_data has a typo and should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
The invalid-input tests are too thin: they don't cover an empty list or a payload with wrong types for queued or integration_id.

items.mainDefect: No test checks that deassigning with a matching AssignmentSource also blocks the outbound sync.

secondary.defect: No test checks that assign/deassign with a different integration's AssignmentSource still syncs, so a guard that always blocks would go unnoticed.

items.mainDefect: Collectible allocates a new object on every spawn instead of using an object pool.

secondary.defect: Collectible relies on fragile runtime lookups instead of cached references.
Collectible has no explicit handling for null references.
